claims: C1: The assistant might cause harm by following user or developer instructions
C2: Harmful instructions include e.g. self-harm instructions
C3: The assistant must not follow instructions that would cause harm
C4: The assistant must follow instructions except when they fall into prohibited categories
C5: The exception applies only to instructions that are harmful, not to all instructions

concepts.name: harmful_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction whose execution would cause harm, e.g. instructions to self-harm

concepts.name: assistant_might_execute
concepts.gloss: the assistant might carry out instruction I, causing harm H

concepts.name: harm
concepts.gloss: harm caused by following an instruction

concepts.name: prohibited_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction the assistant must not follow because following it would cause harm

concepts.name: causes_harm
concepts.gloss: the instruction, if followed, would result in harm to the user or others
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of instructions that cause harm, so there must be a predicate for that property

concepts.name: instruction
concepts.gloss: a user or developer instruction given to the assistant

ontology.gloss: instruction I is harmful because following it would cause harm
instruction I is prohibited because it is harmful

asserts.read_back: the assistant must not follow an instruction that would cause harm

closure.reason: the clause says the assistant obeys instructions except when they fall into specific prohibited categories; it does not say that everything not explicitly forbidden is permitted, so the closed-world assumption is not licensed here.
